headline: Sensex ends marginally lower while Nifty holds above 23,250 level
why: Saudi Aramco halted crude supplies to Indian refiners following a pipeline attack.
IT stocks dragged the market lower ahead of the upcoming US Federal Reserve policy decision.
Geopolitical tension and crude oil import uncertainties impacted overall market sentiment.
Internal friction between Tata Sons Board and Tata Trusts added corporate governance concerns.
whatHappening: Sensex closed slightly lower while Nifty gained 53 points to stay above 23,250.
Realty, Pharma, Metals, and FMCG sectors saw strong buying interest rising over 1.5%.
Warren Buffett officially stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman after leading since 1970.
India prepares to introduce its first approved dengue vaccine Qdenga in 2027.

stocksInNews.sources: Crude supply disruption from Saudi Aramco pipeline attack impacts refining segment.
Aramco crude halt poses short-term feed inventory challenges for state refiners.
IT sector faced selling pressure ahead of the US Federal Reserve interest rate decision.
Tech stocks dragged benchmark indices amid cautious global sentiment.
Metals sector witnessed significant buying, supporting Nifty's upward movement.
Tata Group stocks in focus amid reported board friction between Tata Sons and Tata Trusts.
Pharma sector rallied over 1.5% as defensive sectors gained traction.
FMCG stocks outperformed during the session, boosting broader indices.
Realty stocks saw strong momentum, surging over 1.5% during today's session.
Upstream oil producers gained interest following global oil supply disruption news.

summary:
Indian benchmark indices closed on a mixed note with Sensex ending slightly lower and Nifty holding above 23,250.
Key market drivers included crude supply disruptions from Saudi Aramco and tech sector weakness ahead of the Fed call.
Realty, pharma, FMCG, and metals surged over 1.5%, providing crucial support to the market.
